This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Taipei Songshan Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Taipei Songshan Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/tw/taipei/RCSS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecast models for Shanghai indicate a daily maximum near 29°C on August 12, 2026, with 28–30°C as the most probable range.** This consensus stems from persistent overcast skies, high humidity near 80%, and scattered showers or thunderstorms associated with residual monsoon moisture and the recent passage of Typhoon Dolphin, which brought heavy rain and flooding to the region around August 9–10. These conditions limit solar heating and convective intensification typical of midsummer subtropical highs in the Yangtze River Delta.

Numerical weather prediction outputs, including regional models aligned with China Meteorological Administration guidance, show afternoon temperatures moderated by cloud cover and potential precipitation, preventing the clearer-sky peaks often seen in drier August periods. Historical climatology places average August highs around 31–32°C, but the current pattern aligns with cooler realizations when frontal or convective activity dominates. 

Trader-implied probabilities—concentrated at 29°C (48%) and 28°C (34.5%), with 30°C at 12%—reflect this model agreement and the narrow uncertainty window one day before the event. Any last-minute shifts in shower timing or clearing could nudge the outcome within the 28–30°C band, while extremes remain low-probability given the established moisture regime. Updated model runs and official briefings from the Shanghai Meteorological Service will provide the final calibration ahead of market resolution.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from sources like the BBC and Time and Date indicate Zhengzhou will experience overcast skies, light rain showers, and moderate northerly winds on August 12, limiting solar heating and keeping the daily maximum in the low-to-mid 20s°C range—well below the historical August average high near 31°C. This pattern stems from a transient weather system with high humidity (around 90%+) and potential flash flooding, which enhances evaporative cooling and reduces diurnal temperature range. Trader consensus clusters tightly on 23–25°C outcomes because numerical weather prediction models show only modest differences in exact precipitation timing and cloud thickness, with lower odds assigned to 26°C+ due to minimal warming potential under these conditions. El Niño-related seasonal warming provides broader context but exerts little influence on this short-term local forecast.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment clusters around 28–29°C for Tokyo’s August 13 maximum because short-range models show persistent cloud cover and scattered showers from an approaching typhoon system that is expected to limit daytime heating.** 

Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble runs indicate a daily high near 28–30 °C (roughly 82–86 °F) under overcast skies and frequent showers, with 70 % precipitation probability. This pattern contrasts with Tokyo’s August climatology of 30–32 °C under clearer conditions. The typhoon’s outer bands increase low-level moisture and reduce solar insolation, capping the maximum and shifting probability mass toward the lower end of the historical range. 

Ensemble spread remains modest, but any westward shift or weakening of the system could allow brief clearing and push readings toward 31 °C; conversely, heavier or earlier rainfall would favor 27 °C or below. New JMA and global model updates over the next 24–48 hours will refine cloud timing and directly influence the final distribution.
